title: Keep Track of Covered Ranges With Add, Remove and Ask

concept.title: Store the covered part as a sorted list of disjoint ranges; every operation touches a contiguous block of that list
body: A set of numbers on a line starts empty. Three operations come in turn. **Add `[l, r)`**: every number in the half-open range becomes covered. **Remove `[l, r)`**: every number in the range becomes uncovered. **Ask `[l, r)`**: is **every** number of the range covered? Print the answers to the questions. The coordinates reach 10^9, so we cannot store the numbers one by one.

Keep the covered part as a **sorted list of disjoint half-open ranges**, in which two ranges that touch (like `[1,3)` and `[3,5)`) are merged into one. All three operations affect a **contiguous block** of this list, found with binary search: for **add**, the block of ranges that overlap or touch `[l, r)` is replaced by one merged range `[min(l, first.start), max(r, last.end))`; for **remove**, the ranges that overlap `[l, r)` are replaced by the possibly surviving left piece `[first.start, l)` and right piece `[r, last.end)`; for **ask**, find the last range with `start <= l` and check `end >= r`.

The remove operation is the mirror image: `lo = bisect_right(ends, l)` and `hi = bisect_left(starts, r)` delimit the ranges that really overlap, and the block is replaced by at most two leftover pieces. Because every range is created by one operation and deleted at most once, the list changes by amortised O(1) ranges per operation, and the binary searches cost O(log q), so the total is O(q log q) plus the cost of shifting the list.

statement: A set of numbers is empty at the start. Process `q` operations; each has a type and a half-open range `[l, r)`: 1 = make all numbers of the range covered, 2 = make all numbers of the range not covered, 3 = ask whether all the numbers of the range are covered. Print the answers (YES or NO) to the operations of type 3, in order, separated by spaces.
inputFormat: The first line has `q`: the number of operations.
Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `l` and `r`: the type of the operation and the half-open range `[l, r)`.
outputFormat: Print one YES or NO for every operation of type 3, on one line.
constraints: 1 <= t <= 3 (1 = add the range, 2 = remove the range, 3 = ask whether the range is fully covered)
At least one operation has the type 3.

examples.note: After adding [10,20) the range [14,16) is covered; after removing it [10,14) is still covered but [10,16) is not: YES YES NO.

hints: Keep disjoint ranges sorted and merge ranges that touch.
Use binary search to find the block of ranges an operation touches.
Replace that block by the merged range (add) or by the surviving left and right pieces (remove).

explanation: The covered part is kept as a sorted list of disjoint half-open ranges (touching ranges are merged); each operation replaces a contiguous block of the list found by binary search: one merged range for add, up to two surviving pieces for remove, and a lookup of the last range starting at or before l for ask.
solution.complexity: Time O(q log q) plus shifting, space O(q).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right

q = int(input())
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

starts = []
ends = []
answers = []
for t, l, rr in ops:
    if t == 3:
        i = bisect_right(starts, l) - 1
        answers.append("YES" if i >= 0 and ends[i] >= rr else "NO")
    elif t == 1:
        lo = bisect_left(ends, l)
        hi = bisect_right(starts, rr)
        if lo < hi:
            l = min(l, starts[lo])
            rr = max(rr, ends[hi - 1])
        starts[lo:hi] = [l]
        ends[lo:hi] = [rr]
    else:
        lo = bisect_right(ends, l)
        hi = bisect_left(starts, rr)
        new_starts = []
        new_ends = []
        if lo < hi:
            if starts[lo] < l:
                new_starts.append(starts[lo])
                new_ends.append(l)
            if ends[hi - 1] > rr:
                new_starts.append(rr)
                new_ends.append(ends[hi - 1])
        starts[lo:hi] = new_starts
        ends[lo:hi] = new_ends
print(*answers)
